items.title: The Two-Sided AI Squeeze That Only Travel Faces
items.summary: Travel is the only major industry getting hit from both directions at once: AI search volumes are exploding without converting while total AI token bills internally are rising.

items.title: Accor CEO Bazin’s Final Stretch: An AI Warning and What’s Next for Ennismore
items.summary: CEO Sébastien Bazin said an Ennismore IPO is "one of four or five" possible fates for the lifestyle joint venture. In M&A-speak, that means Accor's board hasn't decided yet.

items.title: Green Aviation Startups Face a Funding Crisis
items.summary: The electric and hybrid plane dream is alive, but the funding model that gets it there still needs to be figured out.

items.title: Why High-Spend First-Timers Could Be a Destination’s Most Expensive Mistake
items.summary: First-timers spend more per trip. Repeat visitors spend less. But the math still favors loyalty.

items.title: Airbnb’s Brian Chesky Is Creating an AI Lab
items.summary: Is Brian Chesky development of a new AI Lab outside of Airbnb an acknowledgement that building AI capabilities within Airbnb hasn't been up to par? Or are some tech developments like AI too large to sit out without having more skin in the game?

items.title: The U.S.’ Own Goal: Why World Cup Expectations Deflated
items.summary: World Cup host cities were promised a once-in-a-generation tourism surge. The lift is real, but some cities’ results are well below expectations.

items.title: Why Hotel AI Keeps Cutting Costs Instead of Making Money
items.summary: AI can't sell what hotel systems can't see. Until room-level data, guest behavior, and service pricing live in one connected system, the industry's AI gains will stay stuck on the cost efficiency side of the ledger.
